relations.subject: n1ql:automatic-workload-repository
relations.evidence: Before AWR can start collecting data, you must configure this location in the [system:awr](#system-awr) catalog. The repository can be a bucket or a collection, but not a scope.

relations.subject: n1ql:automatic-workload-repository
relations.evidence: AWR checks the availability of repository location at the start of each reporting interval. Until this specified location is available, AWR remains in a quiescent (inactive) state. Once the location becomes accessible, AWR transitions to an active state and begins collecting data.

notable_absence.finding: AWR is a performance-diagnostics feature of exactly the kind that is normally Enterprise Edition only in Couchbase Server, and the page carries no ENTERPRISE EDITION badge and no edition statement of any kind. Compare query-settings.md in this same batch, which does badge use_fts, and server/current/learn/security/auditing.md, which badges auditing - so the convention exists and is simply absent here. A Community Edition reader cannot tell from this page whether AWR is available to them. This is the single most useful thing reconciliation could get a doc fix for. Separately, the page states no version gate either, despite being a feature new in 8.0 (see version_finding).

cross_component_finding: The role gate on this page and the role gate on monitoring-n1ql-query.md in this same batch are DIFFERENT roles and must not be merged: query-awr.md requires `query_manage_system_catalog` (write access to system:awr), monitoring-n1ql-query.md requires the 'Query System Catalog' role (`query_system_catalog`, read access to the monitoring keyspaces). server/current/learn/security/roles.md documents both separately ('Query System Catalog (query_system_catalog)' at one heading, 'Query Manage System Catalog (query_manage_system_catalog)' at another), and server/current/n1ql/n1ql-language-reference/auto-update-statistics.md confirms the split behaviourally: 'To execute SELECT on system:aus, you need the query_system_catalog role. To execute UPDATE on system:aus, you need the query_manage_system_catalog role.' Documentation defect: this page's cross-reference for the role points at ../n1ql-intro/sysinfo.md#authentication-and-client-privileges, but that section documents only the **Query System Catalog** role and never mentions query_manage_system_catalog - so the link does not substantiate the claim it is attached to. Also note the naming inconsistency within the doc set itself: this page uses the internal snake_case id (`query_manage_system_catalog`) while monitoring-n1ql-query.md and sysinfo.md use the Title Case display name ('Query System Catalog'), which is exactly the kind of inconsistency that makes automatic role extraction unreliable.
cross_product_finding: The Server and Capella AWR pages are near-identical - the diff is 6 hunks, all of them link targets and API names - which is itself the finding, because AWR is new in Server 8.0 while the Capella page states no version at all. A Capella reader on a cluster built from a pre-8.0 Server base has no way to know whether AWR is present. Concrete divergences: (1) the Capella page's link to the report generator is BROKEN - '[cbqueryreportgen](#cli:cbqueryreportgen.adoc)' and '[Report Generation CLI Tool](#cli:cbqueryreportgen.adoc)' are unresolved Antora xrefs rendered as fragment links, whereas the Server page resolves them to ../../cli/cbqueryreportgen.md. This is why the Capella extraction record minted no tool concept. (2) The Statistics table's 'analogous to' references point at the Data API ('[Data API (Query Service)](../../data-api-reference/index.md#tag/Query)') on Capella and at the Query REST API ('[Query REST API](../../n1ql-rest-query/index.md#Metrics)') on Server - the same 17 statistics, two different access surfaces, which supports keeping api:query-admin-rest-api / capella:data-api distinct. (3) The Capella page links out of the Capella docs into server/ for TTL ('../../../server/current/learn/data/expiration.md'), already flagged by the Capella extraction. (4) Access model: identical prose on both sides names the Server RBAC role `query_manage_system_catalog`, i.e. the Capella page inherits a Server RBAC role name unadapted - the same defect the Capella n1ql-auditing extraction flagged for 'Full Administrator' / 'Local User Security Administrator'.
version_finding: This is the wave's cleanest availableSince case and also its clearest illustration of the gap. AWR is new in Couchbase Server 8.0 on four independent lines of evidence, NONE of which is on the page itself: (1) server/current/n1ql/n1ql-manage/query-awr.md exists but server/7.6/n1ql/n1ql-manage/ contains only index.md, monitoring-n1ql-query.md and query-settings.md - no query-awr.md; server/7.2/n1ql/n1ql-manage/ is empty. (2) server/current/introduction/whats-new.md has a dedicated '#automatic-workload-repository' section calling it 'a new feature'. (3) server/current/release-notes/relnotes.md describes 'The new Query AWR (Automatic Workload Repository) Report Generator tool' under MB-63389. (4) The supporting CLI tool page server/current/cli/cbqueryreportgen.md has no counterpart under server/7.6/cli/. Yet the reference page a user actually lands on carries no version marker at all - no 'Couchbase Server 8.0' badge of the kind query-settings.md puts on the natural* parameters, and no 'available in Couchbase Server 8.0 and later' sentence. The only version-shaped statement on the whole page is a record-format version, not a product version: the snapshot document field **ver** is documented as 'The version of the data record. For this release, the value is always 1.' - 'this release' is unresolvable from the page. Recommendation for reconciliation: availableSince evidence frequently lives in whats-new/relnotes rather than on the feature page, so the extraction schema should allow an evidence provenance field (page vs sibling page) rather than forcing either a fabricated on-page quote or the loss of the relation.
